# Discussions: the categories

GitHub Discussions is on for this repository. Issues are for bugs, change requests and use reports (the three
templates). Everything else goes here. Categories, in the order they are listed:

| Category | Format | What belongs there |
|---|---|---|
| **Announcements** | announcement (maintainers post) | releases, the one line that changed in a rule, dates |
| **Q&A** | question and answer | "how do I make X a heard capability", "why did confirm() say stale_hearing" |
| **Show and tell** | open discussion | what you put Oathline in front of, with the refusals it made (the issue template "Show us your use" is for the ones we may link to) |
| **Ideas** | open discussion | a change that is not yet a change request: adapters, channels, what a renderer should be allowed to do |
| **Attacks** | open discussion | "I think this gets past the rule": a scenario, a sketch of a test; the ones that hold become rows in ATTACKS.md |
| **Voice** | open discussion | spoken approvals: read-backs, corrections mid-sentence, what "heard" should mean on a phone |

Rules for all of them: no secrets, no real customer data, no logs with names in them. A security problem is never a
discussion: SECURITY.md says how to report it privately.
